name: Elasticsearch
model: JSON documents in indexes, full-text search (BM25), aggregations, dense and sparse vector search; query DSL, ES|QL and SQL
engine_note: Apache Lucene: immutable segments written then merged (LSM-like), inverted indexes, doc values columns, HNSW for vectors; translog for durability
consistency: Single-document atomic; no multi-document transactions. Writes fsync the translog on primary and replicas before ack (default index.translog.durability=request). Near real-time: new docs searchable after refresh (about 1 s). Replica reads can lag.

jepsen.finding: Lost inserted and updated documents under several kinds of network partition, including split brain with two primaries.
Still lost documents in every scenario retested (partitions, paused or crashed nodes), though the split-brain window shrank; advice: keep a separate system of record.

scaling: Horizontal: an index is split into primary shards (count set at creation; changing it needs split/shrink or reindex) spread over nodes, each with replica shards; Elastic Cloud Serverless separates storage and compute.
licence: Triple licence: AGPLv3, SSPL 1.0, or Elastic License 2.0 (your choice)

licence_events.event: Elastic announces that from 7.11, Elasticsearch moves from Apache 2.0 to dual SSPL / Elastic License (source-available); AWS forks 7.10.2 as OpenSearch
Elastic adds AGPLv3 as a third licence option next to ELv2 and SSPL, so it is open source again

managed: Elastic Cloud on AWS, Azure and Google Cloud marketplaces
version_note: 8.19.22 (2026-09-23) is a later patch on the older 8.x line; 9.5.4 is the newest version.
reach: Reach for it when users type words and expect ranked, typo-tolerant results with filters and facets, or when you search and aggregate large volumes of logs.
avoid: Avoid as the only copy of data that must not be lost or that needs multi-document transactions; feed it from a primary database instead.
escape: Postgres full-text search is fine to a point; relevance tuning, facets and log-scale search need a dedicated engine.
chat: A search index over message text (keyword plus vector hybrid), rebuilt from the messages table.
notes: Translog quote: default index.translog.durability is request, 'fsync and commit after every request. In the event of hardware failure, all acknowledged writes will already have been committed to disk.' Refresh quote: 'By default, Elasticsearch periodically refreshes indices every second, but only on indices that have received one search request or more in the last 30 seconds.' Jepsen 2015 recap quote: 'store your data in a database with better safety guarantees, and continuously upsert every document from that database into Elasticsearch.' aphyr.com returns HTTP 451 from this network; read via web.archive.org. No jepsen.io analysis of Elasticsearch after 2015. AGPL blog quote: 'we will be adding AGPL as another license option next to ELv2 and SSPL'. licence_class set to copyleft because AGPLv3 is now one of the options (OSI-approved); the default distribution binaries are still under ELv2. Managed list kept to Elastic's own service; Amazon's service is OpenSearch, not Elasticsearch.
